answer: A reputation vine only grows from a staked root: each agent locks a bond to register, and trust extends branch by branch through completed paid work, never by self-declaration. Each epoch a gale of random audits sweeps the network, demanding live proof of past jobs from a sample of branches; any branch that cannot answer is pruned and its bond slashed. A sable ledger records every cut, so a pruned identity cannot re-root under a new name. Forging 1,000 fakes means 1,000 bonds plus surviving 1,000 simultaneous audits — the attacker's cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once.
